paragraphs.text: translated by
1. WHAT God, of those who hear, is he whose well-praised name we may record in this our sacrifice; and how?
paragraphs.original: कथा देवानां कतमस्य यामनि सुमन्तु नाम शृण्वतां मनामहे ।
paragraphs.translit: kathā devānāṃ katamasya yāmani sumantu nāma śṛṇvatāṃ manāmahe |

paragraphs.text: Who will be gracious? Who of many give us bliss? Who out of all the Host will come to lend us aid?
paragraphs.original: को मृळाति कतमो नो मयस्करत्कतम ऊती अभ्या ववर्तति
paragraphs.translit: ko mṛḷāti katamo no mayaskaratkatama ūtī abhyā vavartati

paragraphs.text: 2. The will and thoughts within my breast exert their power: they yearn with love, and fly to all the regions round.
paragraphs.original: क्रतूयन्ति क्रतवो हृत्सु धीतयो वेनन्ति वेनाः पतयन्त्या दिशः ।
paragraphs.translit: kratūyanti kratavo hṛtsu dhītayo venanti venāḥ patayantyā diśaḥ |

paragraphs.text: None other comforter is found save only these: my longings and my hopes are fixt upon the Gods.
paragraphs.original: न मर्डिता विद्यते अन्य एभ्यो देवेषु मे अधि कामा अयंसत
paragraphs.translit: na marḍitā vidyate anya ebhyo deveṣu me adhi kāmā ayaṃsata

paragraphs.text: 3. To Narasamsa and to Pusan I sing forth, unconcealable Agni kindled by the Gods.
paragraphs.original: नरा वा शंसं पूषणमगोह्यमग्निं देवेद्धमभ्यर्चसे गिरा ।
paragraphs.translit: narā vā śaṃsaṃ pūṣaṇamagohyamagniṃ deveddhamabhyarcase girā |

paragraphs.text: To Sun and Moon, two Moons, to Yama in the heaven, to Trita, Vata, Dawn, Night, and the Atvins Twain.
paragraphs.original: सूर्यामासा चन्द्रमसा यमं दिवि त्रितं वातमुषसमक्तुमश्विना
paragraphs.translit: sūryāmāsā candramasā yamaṃ divi tritaṃ vātamuṣasamaktumaśvinā

paragraphs.text: 4. How is the Sage extolled whom the loud singers praise? What voice, what hymn is used to laud Brhaspati?
paragraphs.original: कथा कविस्तुवीरवान्कया गिरा बृहस्पतिर्वावृधते सुवृक्तिभिः ।
paragraphs.translit: kathā kavistuvīravānkayā girā bṛhaspatirvāvṛdhate suvṛktibhiḥ |

paragraphs.text: May Aja-Ekapad with Rkvans swift to hear, and Ahi of the Deep listen unto our call.
paragraphs.original: अज एकपात्सुहवेभिरृक्वभिरहिः शृणोतु बुध्न्यो हवीमनि
paragraphs.translit: aja ekapātsuhavebhirṛkvabhirahiḥ śṛṇotu budhnyo havīmani

paragraphs.text: 5. Aditi, to the birth of Daksa and the vow thou summonest the Kings Mitra and Varuna.
paragraphs.original: दक्षस्य वादिते जन्मनि व्रते राजाना मित्रावरुणा विवाससि ।
paragraphs.translit: dakṣasya vādite janmani vrate rājānā mitrāvaruṇā vivāsasi |

paragraphs.text: With course unchecked, with many chariots Aryaman comes with the seven priests to tribes of varied sort.
paragraphs.original: अतूर्तपन्थाः पुरुरथो अर्यमा सप्तहोता विषुरूपेषु जन्मसु
paragraphs.translit: atūrtapanthāḥ pururatho aryamā saptahotā viṣurūpeṣu janmasu

paragraphs.text: 6. May all those vigorous Coursers listen to our cry, hearers of invocation, speeding on their way;
paragraphs.original: ते नो अर्वन्तो हवनश्रुतो हवं विश्वे शृण्वन्तु वाजिनो मितद्रवः ।
paragraphs.translit: te no arvanto havanaśruto havaṃ viśve śṛṇvantu vājino mitadravaḥ |

paragraphs.text: Winners of thousands where the priestly meed is won, who gather of themselves great wealth in every race.
paragraphs.original: सहस्रसा मेधसाताविव त्मना महो ये धनं समिथेषु जभ्रिरे
paragraphs.translit: sahasrasā medhasātāviva tmanā maho ye dhanaṃ samitheṣu jabhrire

paragraphs.text: 7. Bring ye Purandbi, bring Vayu who yokes his steeds, for friendship bring ye Pusan with your songs of praise:
paragraphs.original: प्र वो वायुं रथयुजं पुरंधिं स्तोमैः कृणुध्वं सख्याय पूषणम् ।
paragraphs.translit: pra vo vāyuṃ rathayujaṃ puraṃdhiṃ stomaiḥ kṛṇudhvaṃ sakhyāya pūṣaṇam |

paragraphs.text: They with one mind, one thought attend the sacrifice, urged by the favouring aid of Savitar the God.
paragraphs.original: ते हि देवस्य सवितुः सवीमनि क्रतुं सचन्ते सचितः सचेतसः
paragraphs.translit: te hi devasya savituḥ savīmani kratuṃ sacante sacitaḥ sacetasaḥ

paragraphs.text: 8. The thrice-seven wandering Rivers, yea, the mighty floods, the forest trees, the mountains, Agni to our aid,
paragraphs.original: त्रिः सप्त सस्रा नद्यो महीरपो वनस्पतीन्पर्वताँ अग्निमूतये ।
paragraphs.translit: triḥ sapta sasrā nadyo mahīrapo vanaspatīnparvatām̐ agnimūtaye |

paragraphs.text: Krsanu, Tisya, archers to our gathering-place, and Rudra strong amid the Rudras we invoke.
paragraphs.original: कृशानुमस्तॄन्तिष्यं सधस्थ आ रुद्रं रुद्रेषु रुद्रियं हवामहे
paragraphs.translit: kṛśānumastṝntiṣyaṃ sadhastha ā rudraṃ rudreṣu rudriyaṃ havāmahe

paragraphs.text: 9. Let the great Streams come hither with their mighty help, Sindhu, Sarasvati, and Sarayu with waves.
paragraphs.original: सरस्वती सरयुः सिन्धुरूर्मिभिर्महो महीरवसा यन्तु वक्षणीः ।
paragraphs.translit: sarasvatī sarayuḥ sindhurūrmibhirmaho mahīravasā yantu vakṣaṇīḥ |

paragraphs.text: Ye Goddess Floods, ye Mothers, animating all, promise us water rich in fatness and in balm.
paragraphs.original: देवीरापो मातरः सूदयित्न्वो घृतवत्पयो मधुमन्नो अर्चत
paragraphs.translit: devīrāpo mātaraḥ sūdayitnvo ghṛtavatpayo madhumanno arcata

paragraphs.text: 10. And let Brhaddiva, the Mother, hear our call, and Tvastar, Father, with the Goddesses and Dames.
paragraphs.original: उत माता बृहद्दिवा शृणोतु नस्त्वष्टा देवेभिर्जनिभिः पिता वचः ।
paragraphs.translit: uta mātā bṛhaddivā śṛṇotu nastvaṣṭā devebhirjanibhiḥ pitā vacaḥ |

paragraphs.text: Rbhuksan, Vaja, Bhaga, and Rathaspati, and the sweet speech of him who labours guard us well!
paragraphs.original: ऋभुक्षा वाजो रथस्पतिर्भगो रण्वः शंसः शशमानस्य पातु नः
paragraphs.translit: ṛbhukṣā vājo rathaspatirbhago raṇvaḥ śaṃsaḥ śaśamānasya pātu naḥ

paragraphs.text: 11. Pleasant to look on as a dwelling rich in food is the blest favour of the Maruts, Rudra's Sons.
paragraphs.original: रण्वः संदृष्टौ पितुमाँ इव क्षयो भद्रा रुद्राणां मरुतामुपस्तुतिः ।
paragraphs.translit: raṇvaḥ saṃdṛṣṭau pitumām̐ iva kṣayo bhadrā rudrāṇāṃ marutāmupastutiḥ |

paragraphs.text: May we be famed among the folk for wealth in kine. and ever come to you, ye Gods, with sacred food.
paragraphs.original: गोभिः ष्याम यशसो जनेष्वा सदा देवास इळया सचेमहि
paragraphs.translit: gobhiḥ ṣyāma yaśaso janeṣvā sadā devāsa iḷayā sacemahi

paragraphs.text: 12. The thought which ye, O Maruts, Indra and ye Gods have given to me, and ye, Mitra and Varuna,-
paragraphs.original: यां मे धियं मरुत इन्द्र देवा अददात वरुण मित्र यूयम् ।
paragraphs.translit: yāṃ me dhiyaṃ maruta indra devā adadāta varuṇa mitra yūyam |

paragraphs.text: Cause this to grow and swell like a milch cow with milk. Will ye not bear away my songs upon your car?
paragraphs.original: तां पीपयत पयसेव धेनुं कुविद्गिरो अधि रथे वहाथ
paragraphs.translit: tāṃ pīpayata payaseva dhenuṃ kuvidgiro adhi rathe vahātha

paragraphs.text: 13. O Maruts, do ye never, never recollect and call again to mind this our relationship?
paragraphs.original: कुविदङ्ग प्रति यथा चिदस्य नः सजात्यस्य मरुतो बुबोधथ । नाभा यत्र प्रथमं संनसामहे तत्र जामित्वमदितिर्दधातु नः
paragraphs.translit: kuvidaṅga prati yathā cidasya naḥ sajātyasya maruto bubodhatha | nābhā yatra prathamaṃ saṃnasāmahe tatra jāmitvamaditirdadhātu naḥ

paragraphs.text: 14. The Mothers, Heaven and Earth, those mighty Goddesses, worthy of sacrifice, ecune with the race of Gods.
paragraphs.original: ते हि द्यावापृथिवी मातरा मही देवी देवाञ्जन्मना यज्ञिये इतः ।
paragraphs.translit: te hi dyāvāpṛthivī mātarā mahī devī devāñjanmanā yajñiye itaḥ |

paragraphs.text: These Two with their support uphold both Gods and men, and with the Fathers pour the copious genial stream.
paragraphs.original: उभे बिभृत उभयं भरीमभिः पुरू रेतांसि पितृभिश्च सिञ्चतः
paragraphs.translit: ubhe bibhṛta ubhayaṃ bharīmabhiḥ purū retāṃsi pitṛbhiśca siñcataḥ

paragraphs.text: 15. This invocation wins all good that we desire Brhaspati, highly-praised Aramati, are here,
paragraphs.original: वि षा होत्रा विश्वमश्नोति वार्यं बृहस्पतिररमतिः पनीयसी ।
paragraphs.translit: vi ṣā hotrā viśvamaśnoti vāryaṃ bṛhaspatiraramatiḥ panīyasī |

paragraphs.text: Even where the stone that presses meath rings loudly out, and where the sages make their voices heard with hymns.
paragraphs.original: ग्रावा यत्र मधुषुदुच्यते बृहदवीवशन्त मतिभिर्मनीषिणः
paragraphs.translit: grāvā yatra madhuṣuducyate bṛhadavīvaśanta matibhirmanīṣiṇaḥ

paragraphs.text: 16. Thus hath the sage, skilled in loud singers' duties, desiring riches, yearning after treasure,
paragraphs.original: एवा कविस्तुवीरवाँ ऋतज्ञा द्रविणस्युर्द्रविणसश्चकानः ।
paragraphs.translit: evā kavistuvīravām̐ ṛtajñā draviṇasyurdraviṇasaścakānaḥ |

paragraphs.text: Gaya, the priestly singer, with his praises and hymns contented the Celestial people.
paragraphs.original: उक्थेभिरत्र मतिभिश्च विप्रोऽपीपयद्गयो दिव्यानि जन्म
paragraphs.translit: ukthebhiratra matibhiśca vipro'pīpayadgayo divyāni janma

paragraphs.text: 17. Thus hath the thoughtful sage the son of Plati, praised you, O Aaiti and all Adityas.
paragraphs.original: एवा प्लतेः सूनुरवीवृधद्वो विश्व आदित्या अदिते मनीषी ।
paragraphs.translit: evā plateḥ sūnuravīvṛdhadvo viśva ādityā adite manīṣī |

paragraphs.text: Men are made rich by those who are Immortal: the Heavenly Folk have been extolled by Gaya.
paragraphs.original: ईशानासो नरो अमर्त्येनास्तावि जनो दिव्यो गयेन
paragraphs.translit: īśānāso naro amartyenāstāvi jano divyo gayena
